claims.text: Conventional near-equiatomic HEAs processed by standard methods have single-phase microstructures.
Tailored heat treatment and deformation can induce a controlled dual-phase or gradient hierarchical microstructure in an HEA.
The tailored process can produce a nanoscale precipitate dispersion within a ductile HEA matrix.
Synchrotron X-ray diffraction, high-resolution electron microscopy, and nanoindentation can be combined for real-time monitoring of the proposed processing route.
The tailored hierarchical microstructure will synergistically improve strength, ductility, Young's modulus, and fracture resistance relative to conventional single-phase HEAs.
The approach requires an alloy system that permits controlled precipitation without excessive phase segregation.
The proposed benefits should apply under room-temperature static and dynamic loading.
Hierarchical phase heterogeneity creates local stress partitioning or constraint within the alloy.
Interfaces between a ductile matrix and hard precipitates create local interfacial strengthening regions.
Engineered microstructural heterogeneity promotes local load sharing.
The heterogeneous architecture delays crack initiation.
Matrix-hard-phase interfaces enable simultaneous improvements in stiffness, toughness, and strength.
Young's modulus and toughness will improve by approximately 20–30% relative to state-of-the-art HEAs.
The process will retain or enhance ductility and fracture resistance while increasing strength.
Conventionally processed near-equiatomic single-phase HEAs typically exhibit trade-offs among strength, ductility, modulus, and fracture resistance.
Severe elemental segregation can prevent the proposed method from improving properties.
The proposed improvements may not occur if processing leaves the microstructure homogeneous.
Diffusion conditions that prevent precipitation or cause precipitate coarsening can eliminate the expected improvements.
An improvement of less than approximately 20% in key properties such as Young's modulus and fracture toughness would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure to observe the expected nanoscale-precipitate hierarchical microstructure would falsify the hypothesis.
